A patch release for one thing: **0.2.0's Javadoc jar was empty**, and this
restores it. If you are already on 0.2.0 the code is identical — upgrade only if
you want working API documentation in your IDE or on javadoc.io.

## The Javadoc jar

0.2.0 published a 532-byte javadoc jar containing four entries and no
documentation at all, against 1.47 MB and 504 files in 0.1.25. Its only content
was an empty `src/in.vidyalai.claude.sdk/` directory.

That directory is the modular-javadoc output layout, and it is the tell.
`maven-javadoc-plugin` reads `Automatic-Module-Name` out of the jar plugin's
manifest entries, concludes the project is a named module, and switches to
modular processing. This SDK has no `module-info.java`, so the plugin then found
nothing to document, reported

```
error: No source files for package in.vidyalai.claude.sdk.types
```

and wrote an empty jar. `failOnError=false` — set long before this, so that a
doc warning could never fail a release — meant the build stayed green while
publishing it.

`Automatic-Module-Name` arrived in 0.2.0 to give JPMS consumers a stable module
name instead of one derived from the jar filename. It keeps that job here:
`legacyMode=true` holds the plugin on non-modular processing, so the jar is back
to 1.36 MB and 495 files **and** the manifest still carries the module name. The
two were never actually in tension.

Maven Central artifacts cannot be replaced, so 0.2.0's javadoc jar stays empty.
That is the whole reason this release exists.

## Also

The release workflow's `softprops/action-gh-release` step moved from `v2` to
`v3`. The `v2` tag is pinned to the 2.x line, which still declares
`using: node20`; GitHub-hosted runners now force those onto Node 24 and warn,
and once the forcing stops the step breaks rather than warns. `v3.0.0` changed
the runtime and nothing else. No effect on the published artifacts.
